newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian term lenders to come under SLR - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Indian term lenders to come under SLR - newspaper.

text.p: Indian term-lending financial institutions will be required to maintain a statutory liquidity ratio (SLR), a newspaper quoted Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor Chakravarty Rangarajan as saying.

The SLR will require term-lenders to invest a certain percentage of their deposits in government securities and approved securities as specified by the central bank, Rangarajan told The Financial Express newspaper in an interview published in its Tuesday edition.
Rangarajan said financial institutions will be brought under the liquidity net before the credit policy for the second half of 1997/98 (April-March) is announced.

"The (term-lending financial) institutions are very large and have their own position in the financial system," Rangarajan said. "We will work out some requirements regarding the maintenance of liquidity ratios."
"CRR (cash reserve ratio) is basically a monetary tool while SLR is a liquidity requirement," he was quoted as saying.
"Something around these lines can be worked out in regard to financial institutions soon ..much before the next credit policy," the RBI chief said.
The credit policy for the second half of the year is normally announced around October.
Replying to a question on interest rates, Rangarajan said short-term interest rates had already fallen sharply and long-term rates will follow if inflation remains low.
"The point is that one has to ensure that inflation remains at a low level for a considerable period of time," the RBI chief said. "Only then can inflationary expectations be broken."

He said the yield on 91-day treasury bills had fallen from 12.36 percent last May to 6.21 percent this year. Similarly yields on the 364-day bills had fallen from 12.94 percent to 8.97 percent in the same period, he told the newspaper.
"The process (of falling interest rates) begins at the short end and filters through to the other maturities," Rangarajan said.
